This message comes from Schwab.
Investing with Schwab is like a hike with endless trails.
Go solo with self-directed investing,
take stops along the way with trading,
or choose a guide with full service wealth management.
Whatever trails you take,
you can invest your way with Schwab.
This is NPR News Now.
The latest headlines every hour.
Live from NPR News in Washington, I'm Rylan Barton.
President Trump is in Southern China,
where he's scheduled to hold his first trilateral meeting
with China's Xi Jinping and Russia's Vladimir Putin.
NPR's Franco Ordonez reports Trump wants to discuss
nuclear arms control and help with Iran.
It'll be the first time the three leaders
who manage the world's biggest nuclear arsenal
sit down together.
There are questions about what substance
will come out of the meetings,
especially when China has shown little interest
in reducing its nuclear weapons.
But this gathering, like many gatherings of foreign leaders,
is also about the photo op.
It's a chance to demonstrate Trump's influence abroad
after the devastating midterm elections.
Trump wants to be seen as a president
who can pick up the phone and get America's biggest adversaries
around a table to get things done.
The test is whether Trump's personalized form
of diplomacy will work,
especially when he's been politically weakened back home.
Franco Ordonez, NPR News.
Congressman Hakeem Jeffries has been nominated
for House Speaker when the Democrats take control
of Congress in January, NPR's Claudia Grisales reports.
House Democrats voted during a closed-door meeting,
251 to 11, in support of Hakeem Jeffries' nomination.
Afterwards, the current House Minority Leader
told reporters his caucus will work to deliver
for the American people.
Our job is to fight MAGA extremism, not each other,
to fight MAGA extremism, and to get big things done.
Several incoming, more left-wing House members
who did not support Jeffries' bid said they're still pushing
for a more aggressive agenda to address affordability,
immigration, and other issues.
The House floor will hold its vote for Speaker
on the first day of the new Congress next year,
on January 3rd.
Claudia Grisales, NPR News, the Capitol.
A slew of recent digital service disruptions
affecting everything from Microsoft Outlook
to flight communications are wreaking havoc
across the Internet, but experts tell NPR's
Jenna McLaughlin that there's no evidence
cyberattacks are to blame.
The National Security Agency financial executives
and others have told Congress that a series
of recent service outages affecting
the NSA's classified networks, banking applications,
and other digital services are the result
of technical glitches caused by a large volume
of critical updates to systems.
That's according to a congressional source
not authorized to speak on the record.
With the advent of artificial intelligence,
it's becoming easier and faster
to find vulnerabilities in systems.
Companies are being forced to rapidly patch
those holes to prevent attacks,
but sometimes those patches are difficult to apply
or cause unintended disruptions.
Cybersecurity experts tell NPR the Internet
has always been fragile, and the industry
is still adjusting to the pace of updates
in the age of AI.
Jenna McLaughlin, NPR News.
Major U.S. stock indexes closed mix today
as AI stocks kept swinging on uncertainty
about how much strength is left in the AI boom.
The S&P 500 fell nearly a quarter percent.
That makes us NPR.
El Salvador's president, Naib Bukele,
says that his troops have demolished
the lavish home of a prominent gang leader in Haiti.
It wasn't immediately clear if he was killed.
Bukele described the attack as a gift
to the Haitian people on the anniversary
of the Battle of Verteares.
The 1803 battle helped secure Haiti's independence
from France as it became the world's first
black republic.
Muslims are expected to outnumber Christians
by the year 2035, according to Pew Research.
NPR's Jason Derose reports.
Pew projects that by the year 2070,
Christians will decline to less than half
of the U.S. population, though they'll remain
the country's largest single religious group.
At the same time, religiously unaffiliated people
will rise to just over 40 percent,
mostly due to people leaving Christianity.
Currently, Judaism is the largest non-Christian religion
in the U.S., but researchers say that by 2070,
Jews will be outnumbered by both Muslims
and Hindus in this country if recent
demographic trends continue.
Globally, Pew projects that more than half
of the world's Christians will live in sub-Saharan Africa
by the year 2070, largely due to higher birth rates there.
Jason Derose, NPR News.
- During President Trump's visit to the Philippines,
President Ferdinand Marcos Jr. says he sent a delivery
of jollibee fried chicken to Trump
so he could have a taste of Manila.
Jollibee is a popular local fast food chain
that's known for its fried chicken.
It's also become a feature of regional diplomacy.
Australian Prime Minister Anthony Albanese
visited a jollibee branch in Manila this week.
I'm Rylan Barton, and you're listening
to NPR News from Washington.
- This message comes from Cure Alzheimer's Fund.
From family to community,
connections and the memories they make are everything.
The hugs, the strolls, the laughs, songs, and dreams.
Cure Alzheimer's Fund empowers the scientists
who dedicate their lives to curing Alzheimer's disease.
Great progress has been made and the momentum is building.
There is more to do.
Learn more at curealz.org.
Let's keep our memories together.

El Salvador's Nayib Bukele says troops demolished a gang leader's lavish home in Haiti
